espn-603994.headline: Brex rates South Africa's centres best. He can't face them
beats: Italy are without Tommaso Menoncello, out for 12 weeks with a shoulder hurt playing for Toulouse, and Nacho Brex, who detached a bicep in the last round of the Top 14. They are two of 16 Italians unavailable through injury.

Brex calls Damian de Allende and Jesse Kriel "probably the best centre partnership in the world". Italy's July midfield, with or without him, let in 47 against New Zealand and 57 against Australia a week later.

South Africa came off scoring six tries in Australia and still lost 38–42. They sit level on points with New Zealand at the top, and an Italy win would put them second in the world rankings behind them.
Italy beat South Africa 20–18 in Florence ten years ago this month. Quesada says his side must be unpredictable this time, which a rebuilt midfield at least makes easier.

espn-603995.headline: Scotland have drawn with New Zealand twice since 1905
beats: New Zealand have won the other 31 of their 33 meetings. The last, on 8 November 2025 with Scotland at home, ended 17–25. The hosts fell 17–0 behind, came back to 17–17, then watched Damian McKenzie settle it late.

Since then Scotland have put 50 on France and seven tries on Argentina. New Zealand lost three in a row to South Africa, then scored 50 and 43 against Australia in October. Win, and Scotland go up to fifth in the world, above England.

Jack Dempsey has the candid version of his side: "We can be the best team in the world for 20 minutes and we can be the worst team in the world for 20 minutes." Three of the last four defeats to New Zealand were by eight points, which is roughly what the other 20 minutes cost.

espn-603996.headline: One point split them last year. It still might.
beats: Wales beat Japan 24–23 in Cardiff on 15 November 2025. A year on they sit 10th and 12th in the world, and one point apart in the Nations Championship.

Wales have not played since July, when they lost 21–35 to Argentina and then 0–43 to South Africa without a try. Japan lost 28–34 at home to Fiji on 24 October, having beaten the same side 20–15 in September.

Japan are without their first three choices at flyhalf: two are injured, and Ryunosuke Ito, who started every Test this year, is back at university. Wales have a choice instead, and start Sam Costelow ahead of Dan Edwards.
Eddie Jones calls it a "fantastic opportunity". A Japan win by any margin lifts them to 10th and drops Wales to 12th at best. The loser's reward is New Zealand or England a week later.

espn-603997.headline: France get their halves back; Fiji borrow from England
beats: Antoine Dupont and Romain Ntamack start together at half-back for the first time since March 2025. Dupont missed all of July with a calf problem. The France side that toured without them lost by two in Christchurch, then put 42 points on both Australia and Japan.
Fiji's July included an 8–73 home defeat to England. Jake White, in his second game in charge, now gives a Test debut to Nathan Hughes, a former England international.
Fiji did beat Japan 34–28 in their last game, and a win in Lyon would drop France to fifth in the world, below England. Last November France beat them 34–21 at home.
France have South Africa at home the following week. The reunited halves get one game to remember how it works.

espn-603998.headline: England's senior players back Borthwick. Now they must win
beats: Maro Itoje and Jamie George called a squad meeting on Friday over a Times article portraying players fed up with Steve Borthwick. George: "When someone comes at one of our own, we are going to fight to protect them." Ellis Genge, said to have clashed with Borthwick, is on the bench.

Australia arrive having conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand in a fortnight, a month after scoring 42 against South Africa. Beat England by any margin and they go fifth in the world, with England down to seventh behind them and Scotland.
Ben Curry starts after an injury-hit 16 months, in for his injured twin Tom, with the job of slowing Fraser McReight on his 50th cap. Fin Smith is passed fit at fly-half after a calf injury.
The RFU chief executive, Bill Sweeney, has backed Borthwick through to next year's World Cup. That settles who coaches England, not how they play on Sunday.

espn-603999.headline: The No 1 ranking comes to Saint-Denis on loan
beats: South Africa have been first in the world since 31 August. They lead the Nations Championship log on points difference alone, level with New Zealand, and a France win would hand the ranking to New Zealand too.
Their last game was a 42–38 defeat in Australia: six tries scored and still not enough. Their last visit to France, on 8 November 2025, went better, 32–17.

France spent July without their Toulouse and Montpellier players and still lost to New Zealand by only 34–32. For Fiji in Lyon, Antoine Dupont and Romain Ntamack were picked to start together at half-back for the first time since March 2025.
South Africa go to Ireland on 21 November. Ireland are the side France pass in the rankings with a win here, so somebody arrives in that game with a grievance.

espn-604000.headline: Italy have not won since they beat England
beats: That was 23–18 at home in March. Since then Italy have lost four running, conceding 57 to Australia and 47 to New Zealand in July, and they sit on zero points.
Argentina have the opposite problem. Their last three defeats were all by seven points or fewer, and their last game was a 28–28 draw with Australia. Staying close is not what is going wrong.
Italy went into November with 16 players injured, centres Nacho Brex and Tommaso Menoncello among them. Win anyway and they climb to ninth in the world, above Wales and Fiji.
A week later Fiji come to Italy, also on zero points. One of these two games has to go right.

espn-604001.headline: A Welsh hat trick last time still lost by 26
beats: Tom Rogers became the first Wales player to score a hat trick against New Zealand in Cardiff last November. New Zealand crossed seven times, won 52–26 and extended a winning streak over Wales that was reported at 72 years.
Both sides have conceded 43 to South Africa this year. New Zealand scored 28 that day. Wales, in July, scored none, and have not played since.

New Zealand lost three straight to South Africa, then put seven tries on Australia in each of the next two games. They sit level on points with South Africa at the top of the Nations Championship, where first meets second on finals weekend.
Wales are ninth of twelve, and a win would lift them above Fiji to ninth in the world. Getting there takes more than one man scoring three tries.

espn-604002.headline: The quiet week before New Zealand has the steep drop
beats: Japan arrive in London 12th in the world, seven places below England. The next visitors are New Zealand, which makes this the one England are expected to get through. Lose it and they fall to 7th, below Scotland and Australia.
England need no reminder of how that goes. They lost 18–23 in Italy in March. Japan scored 63 and 57 in September, then lost 28–34 to Fiji six weeks after beating them.

Steve Borthwick goes in under scrutiny after a Times report of player unrest over his leadership at the end of the summer tour in Argentina. Jamie George said the squad were "really upset" by it. Ben Curry has taken his injured twin Tom's place, with concerns that Tom may miss the whole Nations Championship.
Japan go on to Scotland. England host New Zealand, which is no week to be explaining a loss to Japan.

espn-604003.headline: Win and Ireland stay put. Anything less costs a place.
beats: Ireland have been third in the world since 13 July, and no winning margin here moves them an inch. A draw is enough to drop them below France.

Fiji are bottom of the Nations Championship, without a point from three games, and conceded 73 to England at home in July. Their last result was a 34–28 win over Japan on 24 October. Upsets have been built on less.
Joey Carbery won the last of his 38 caps against Fiji, in 2022. His case for a recall now runs through Fiji A in Cork on 20 November, a reminder that Ireland are counting depth as well as results.
Six days later, South Africa, the table leaders, come to Dublin. Fiji go to Italy, the only other side without a point. Each side will know which of its next two games it can afford to lose.

espn-604004.headline: Two sides that play in flashes, one place apart
beats: Jack Dempsey says Scotland can be the "best team in the world for 20 minutes", and the worst for another twenty. The Guardian says much the same of Australia: flickers and sparks, rarely sustained long enough to win, then win again in the next Test.

The evidence runs both ways. Scotland put 50 on France and seven tries on Argentina, then lost 43–21 away to Ireland. Australia beat South Africa 42–38 in September, then conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand inside a fortnight.
The rankings will reward whoever keeps it up longest. A Scotland win lifts them to fifth, above England, and keeps Australia behind them in the Nations Championship table.

Australia won 16 straight in this fixture after 1982. Gregor Townsend, who once spent a summer playing club rugby in Sydney, has since made it the source of some of his side's most scintillating rugby.
